recent_articles.title: Meta and Snapchat blocking Saudi dissidents’ accounts | Social media | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Meta**, **Instagram**, and **X** have blocked accounts of Saudi Arabian dissidents, following orders from the Saudi government. The move has been met with criticism from human rights groups who argue that these companies are effectively silencing dissent and aiding in repression.  At least seven accounts were blocked by **Meta** at the end of April, including those of two American citizens and two individuals based in Europe. **Snapchat** appears to have slowed or removed some accounts without notifying users, while **X**, owned by **Elon Musk**, has informed some users that their content was blocked due to a request from the Saudi government.

recent_articles.title: 'Go home' for Green Card rule: Immigration attorney Rahul Reddy explains what H-1B visa holders should do now - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **USCIS** has issued a new memo that requires individuals seeking Green Cards to apply for visas in their home countries instead of adjusting status within the United States. The memo, which experts say may be challenged in court, emphasizes that approving Green Card applications from within the US is a "favor" and not a right.  The memo's impact on those who have already filed Green Card applications remains unclear, but it suggests individuals with pending I-140 petitions should consult legal counsel to strengthen their case.

recent_articles.title: US stocks today: Dow hits record high as Middle East hopes lift sentiment and Warsh takes Fed charge - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **S&P 500** closed at a new high, marking its eighth consecutive weekly gain.  **Semiconductor stocks** were mostly higher, driven by gains in Qualcomm and Lenovo Group's strong quarterly results. The **Federal Reserve** welcomed new Chair **Kevin Warsh**, while **Estee Lauder** rose after ending merger talks with **Puig**.   The **U.S.** made progress toward a deal with **Iran**, though more work remains according to **Secretary of State Marco Rubio**.

recent_articles.title: Will TVK government take ‘firm stand’ on Mekedatu project, asks Palaniswami - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Edappadi K. Palaniswami**, general secretary of the **AIADMK**, questioned the **Tamil Nadu** government's ability to protect its interests in the **Mekedatu balancing reservoir project** on the Cauvery river, citing the reported support of the **Congress** party and concerns about potential power-sharing agreements.  **D.K. Shivakumar**, Karnataka’s Deputy Chief Minister, reportedly stated that Tamil Nadu had no right to object to the project, while **T.T.V. Dhinakaran**, founder of the **AMMK**, echoed these concerns.

recent_articles.title: What else does U.S. have in store for India’s foreign policy? asks Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** general secretary Jairam Ramesh questioned **U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's** future plans for Indian foreign policy, citing Rubio's recent announcements regarding a Venezuelan presidential visit to India and the postponement of the event due to an Ebola outbreak in Africa.  Ramesh expressed concern over **Rubio's** repeated pre-emptive pronouncements on India's foreign policy decisions, including the halt of Operation Sindoor.

recent_articles.title: Congress leader Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan elected Kerala Speaker - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan**, a senior Congress leader, was elected as the Speaker of the 16th Kerala Legislative Assembly on Friday (May 22, 2026). He won with 101 votes, defeating **A.C. Moideen** and **B.B. Gopakumar**.  The election took place after **G. Sudhakaran**, the previous Pro Tem Speaker, chose not to vote.  **V.D. Satheesan**, the Chief Minister, and **Pinarayi Vijayan**, the Leader of the Opposition, led Radhakrishnan to the Speaker's chair.

recent_articles.title: States should be allowed to conduct CET for medical courses: CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** called for the decentralization of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) and urged **States** to have the opportunity to conduct their own Common Entrance Tests (CET) for medical courses. He argued that education is a concurrent list subject, allowing states to independently administer entrance exams for professional courses within the federal system.

recent_articles.title: DMK faces a challenge as allies set to join TVK government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DMK**, the Secular Progressive Alliance's leader since 2017, has lost most of its pre-poll allies.  The party is now left with only **MDMK** and **Manithaneya Makkal Katchi**, who contested on its Rising Sun symbol. Additionally, the DMDK remains loyal to the TVK government. The Congress abandoned the DMK after the Assembly polls and joined Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's Cabinet on Thursday, while the IUML and VCK are expected to join the Ministry on Friday.

recent_articles.title: Historic shift: Vijay’s Cabinet marks Tamil Nadu’s best SC representation till date - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has appointed seven members from the Scheduled Caste (SC) community to his Cabinet. This marks a significant increase in SC representation compared to previous Cabinets.  Political analyst Stalin Rajangam believes this is a positive step towards inclusivity and sets a benchmark for future governments. However, Punitha Pandiyan, former Vice President of the Tamil Nadu SC/ST Commission, argues that celebrating this development trivializes SC politics.

recent_articles.title: Congress workers clash with police in Jaipur during stir against NEET-UG paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** party workers clashed with **police** in **Rajasthan** on Thursday during a protest against the NEET-UG exam paper leak.  Led by **State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra**, the protesters demanded the resignation of **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and the dissolution of the **National Testing Agency**. The demonstrators, carrying banners and placards, were forcibly dispersed using water cannons. Some protesters suffered minor injuries.

recent_articles.title: Himachal urban poll results reflect public confidence in Congress; party united with no groupism, says CM Sukhu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu**, Chief Minister of **Himachal Pradesh**, attributed the Congress-backed candidates' victory in recent urban local body elections to public approval of the party's governance. He highlighted the sustained popularity despite anti-incumbency pressures and emphasized a unified effort among party workers.  He also criticized the BJP for its perceived lack of support for Himachal Pradesh, particularly regarding issues like the Revenue Deficit Grant and natural disasters. Sukhu asserted that the Congress has fulfilled its promises and exceeded expectations in delivering on commitments such as welfare schemes and reforms in education and healthcare.

recent_articles.title: From rallies to reels: political catchphrases turn dance anthems in Kolkata - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A new genre of political techno remixes has emerged in Kolkata, using catchy hooks and meme-friendly punchlines to criticize politicians. The trend began with songs like "Khela Hobe" and continues with remixed versions of "Hamba Hamba", "Mach Chor", and "File Chor". These songs often target specific individuals or parties, gaining popularity through social media platforms like Instagram and YouTube Shorts.  The use of crude humor and satirical lyrics reflects a culture of insult-flinging on social media while also expressing anger towards political leaders who abuse power.

recent_articles.title: Chennithala seeks report on parole granted to Periye murder convicts - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following protests from the families of the victims in the Periye twin murder case, **Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala** has requested a report on the parole granted to five convicts. The parole order was issued during the final phase of the previous Left Democratic Front government's tenure and the jail authorities clarified that prisoners are generally not allowed to leave during elections.  The family members of the victims plan to meet the Chief Minister and the Home Minister to file a formal complaint against the mass parole granted to the convicts.

recent_articles.title: I am from India but none of my firm partners is Indian: Attorney Rahul Reddy counters hate on social media - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Reddy**, an immigration attorney, and **Emily Neumann**, a partner at his firm, the Reddy-Neumann Brown PC, addressed concerns about the "Indians only hire Indians" narrative circulating on social media. They emphasized that while fraud exists within the H-1B program, it does not represent the entire process or all individuals involved.  **Dr. Sean Wang**, a Chinese-American assistant professor, also filed a lawsuit against **Southern Methodist University**, alleging preferential treatment of Indian employees by head of the department **Dr. Hemang Desai**.

recent_articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar challenges BJP leaders to travel by public transport daily - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, Deputy Chief Minister of **Karnataka**, criticized **BJP** leaders for using public transport only for photoshoots in response to the Prime Minister's call for austerity measures. He challenged them to travel by public transport daily, questioning the sincerity of their actions.  He also addressed the Prime Minister's call to abstain from buying gold and expressed his commitment to visit Delhi when called upon by **Rahul Gandhi**, Leader of the Opposition.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Cabinet expansion LIVE: Congress set to join Tamil Nadu’s first coalition government in decades - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** is set to expand his Cabinet with the oath of office for 23 new ministers scheduled for Thursday, May 21, 2026.  The ceremony will take place at **Lok Bhavan**. The Congress party, which won five seats in the alliance led by the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, is joining the coalition government. **Thol. Thirumavalavan**, leader of the VCK, and the **IUML** have been invited to join the Council of Ministers.

recent_articles.title: PM busy handing out candies in Italy amid economic storm at home, says Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** president Mallikarjun Kharge and **Rahul Gandhi** criticized the **Narendra Modi** government's economic policies, accusing it of prioritizing publicity over addressing rising inflation, unemployment, and weakening economic indicators.  **Kharge** highlighted the increase in average debt per Indian and wealth concentration among billionaires, while **Gandhi** criticized the Prime Minister's focus on foreign trips during a time of economic distress. Congress officials also pointed to the rupee's decline, falling foreign exchange reserves, and large investor outflows as evidence of government mismanagement.

recent_articles.title: Modi, Shah are traitors who are attacking the Constitution, says Rahul at Rae Bareli meet - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress** party, criticized **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** and **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, accusing them of attacking the Constitution and supporting industrialists. He also warned of an impending economic crisis, stating that it would disproportionately affect ordinary citizens while benefiting those in power.  Gandhi unveiled a statue of Veera Pasi in Rae Bareli, highlighting his party's renewed focus on the community. He further criticized the BJP government over land acquisition policies and unemployment rates, vowing to fight for the rights of the people.

recent_articles.title: TACO abroad, boss at home: Trump may be losing against China or Iran, but still controls MAGA | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump**'s foreign policy, particularly his handling of the Iran conflict, has led to a mixed bag of results. While he may be losing public support and facing congressional rebuke, he remains powerful within the Republican Party. **Trump's** tactics of intimidation have proven effective in silencing dissenters, as evidenced by the defeat of **Rep. Thomas Massie**, who lost his primary election after refusing to pledge unwavering loyalty. This strategy has also led to a decline in public approval ratings and fueled concerns about his ability to lead effectively.  Despite these challenges, **Trump** continues to hold significant sway within the Republican Party, demonstrating that loyalty trumps ideology and seniority in American politics.

recent_articles.title: Full list of Kerala Cabinet Ministers by May 17, says Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, the newly appointed Chief Minister of Kerala, indicated that the full list of Ministers will be presented to **Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar** by Sunday evening.  The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for Monday at 10 a.m., with speculation surrounding potential ministerial appointments within the **United Democratic Front (UDF)**. Senior Congress leader **Ramesh Chennithala**, reportedly disgruntled over not being chosen as Chief Minister, is rumored to be joining the Cabinet as Home Minister.  **K.C. Venugopal**, an aspirant for the CM's post, also met with Mr. Chennithala in conciliatory talks. The UDF is expected to finalize its ministerial appointments after discussions with all partners.

recent_articles.title: Bidadi township: Deve Gowda announces stir against project; DKS hits back - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **H.D. Deve Gowda**, former Prime Minister, launched a campaign against the proposed Bidadi township project, claiming it targets fertile agricultural land and is driven by a "land business." He accused the **Siddaramaiah** government of facilitating this project under the guise of urban development, drawing parallels with previous satellite township projects that were withdrawn due to public opposition. **D.K. Shivakumar**, Deputy Chief Minister, countered Gowda's accusations, alleging that the Kumaraswamy family amassed wealth through real estate dealings and initiated similar projects in the past.
